items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Tiger Joe somebody on the drums here and get some people from the Philharmonic on the violins

ctx.x: One thing that's puzzling, I was just reading in that magazine, Billboard over there, the sales of that pop thing are down, these little record companies are firing about 1,000 people, but the jazz and classical are holding their own. They never were that big, but they don't have a big dip in jazz and classical sales -- but the pop companies are really having headaches with sales. Now, the guys who were selling gold records a year or two ago can't give their stuff away right now. They were working with the fad at…

Just like with the disco -- the disco music with that heavy beat, you know, getting the string sections from the New York Philharmonic, putting a rock rhythm section behind it -- you know, no musician in their right mind would ever do that! A businessman would, though; he say5/ well, that will sell, so do it. Tiger Joe somebody on the drums here and get some people from the Philharmonic on the violins -- because that might sell, see. But a musician wouldn't do that. That's the type of music they been producing…
